speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia A

The patient's age (18-month-old male), spontaneous hemarthrosis without trauma, prolonged ACT, and family history involving maternal uncles are classic indicators of a genetic bleeding disorder. The specific pattern of isolated prolonged aPTT/ACT with normal PT strongly supports a deficiency in Factor VIII (Hemophilia A) rather than Hemophilia B or other causes. Given the clear clinical evidence, further testing is not required for the diagnosis.
